drawings.description: un dessin : deux cônes opposés par leur base, la base étant un disque hachuré — la suspension au sens usuel ; à côté, son avatar combinatoire, un losange de quatre sommets, légendé $(X,e)$ avec une flèche vers $e$
drawings.kind: suspension: two cones on a hatched disc; rhombus (X, e)
drawings.notes: Two cones opposed by their base, the base a hatched disc (ellipse), the upper apex joined by a vertical stroke to a point of the base, a dotted stroke to the lower apex; beside it the combinatorial avatar, a rhombus of four vertices with a heavy dot at the left vertex, labelled (X, e) with an arrow to e.

drawings.description: feuillet de croquis : rien n'y est rédigé
drawings.kind: sheet of sketches: X x Y, diamond X0..X3, X -> X x I, long pencil curves
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop. The rest of the sheet: X x Y with an arrow down-left; the diamond X_0, X_1, X_2, X_3 (X_0 -> X_1, X_1 -> X_3, X_2 -> X_3, and a stroke from X_2 towards X_0 with no head); X -> X x I and x_0 x I; the long pencil curves crossing the sheet: one at the left in two pieces (broken at the label X x Y), one through the middle passing beside the diamond, one at the right. The arrows are separate strokes between the labels, as on the page (no vertex is drawn). Left out: the scribbled, struck "x_0, y" near the middle. The cones, the rhombus and (X, e) belong to 04-1; the "Sigma^1 X" written above the cones (the suspension the cones depict) is drawn in neither record: to check whether it belongs to 04-1. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): « Sigma^1 X » is set in the transcription as a displayed formula before the mark of 04-1, so it is text and belongs to neither drawing. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: à gauche du feuillet, un grand croquis que le texte ne décrit pas : au bord gauche, deux petits triangles hachurés marqués $B$ et $C$ ; deux longs traits partis du bord gauche se croisent et aboutissent l'un à « $\beta$ », l'autre à « $\gamma$ » ; une courbe rejoint $\beta$ par le haut, et un trait double descend de $\gamma$ vers le bas à gauche.
drawings.kind: two hatched regions B, C and two crossing lines to beta and gamma
drawings.notes: Not described in the transcription (found on the facsimile; it illustrates the last paragraph, on B, C, beta, gamma). Two small hatched triangles on the left edge of the sheet, cut by the edge, labelled B and C. Two long strokes start at the left edge, cross at one computed point, and end one at beta (upper right), the other at gamma (lower right); a curve comes down to beta from the upper left; from the end point at gamma a doubled stroke goes down to the lower left, off the crop. The hatching of the two triangles is placed by eye. The oblique writing at the lower right of the crop is text and is not drawn; the small arrow diagram B, C -> o -> beta, gamma at the bottom left of the sheet is a relation to be set as text. The sheet is a printed form (letterhead of a school inspectorate, no private name); the typed text is not drawn. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the redraw matches the page; nothing corrected. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.
